fixes.target: figure-45: Excavation planning process
fixes.value: Flow chart of the excavation planning process: 'Excavation planned', then 'Refer to plans of buried services', then 'Use locating devices', then 'Services located and confirmed by trial holes as necessary?'; if No, 'Is there a reasonable explanation for not being located?*' (No leads to 'Contact owners of services†'; Yes leads to 'Dig as many trial holes as necessary by hand', then 'Services exposed?', where No leads to 'Contact owners of services†'). If services are located, or exposed (Yes), the next question is 'Evidence of other services?**'; Yes leads to 'Obtain more information and plans if possible' and back to 'Use locating devices', and No leads to 'Is work close to the services?', where Yes means 'Carry out excavation near services by hand digging' and No means 'Use tools of choice'. Footnotes: * for example, could services be non-metallic pipes; ** in particular visual evidence, eg service connections; † if owners cannot be traced despite all reasonable attempts, excavation could proceed using hand-dug trial holes and great care.
fixes.reason: Flow chart steps and branches read from the image in order, with footnotes summarised.
fixes.evidence: Boxes 'Excavation planned', 'Refer to plans of buried services', 'Use locating devices', Yes/No arrows, footnotes *, **, †, caption 'Figure 45 Excavation planning process'.

fixes.target: figure-47: Typical locations for the most common asbestos-containing materials
fixes.value: Cut-away line drawing of a multi-storey building with 39 numbered coloured markers showing typical locations of the most common asbestos-containing materials, grouped in a key as: Roof and exterior walls (1 Roof sheets, slates and tiles; 2 Guttering and drainpipe; 3 Wall cladding; 4 Soffit boards; 5 Panel beneath window; 6 Roofing felt and coating to metal wall cladding), Boiler, vessels and pipe work (7-13, eg lagging, gaskets, rope seals, boiler flue), Ceilings (14 Spray coating; 15 Loose asbestos in ceiling/floor cavity; 16 Tiles, slats, canopies and firebreaks above ceilings; 17 Textured coatings and paints), Interior walls/panels (18-29, eg partition walls, panel lining to lift shaft, fire door, bath panel). Further groups are Flooring materials (30 Floor tiles, linoleum and paper backing, lining to suspended floor), Air handling systems (31 Lagging; 32 Gaskets; 33 Anti-vibration gaiter), Domestic appliances (34-36, eg gaskets in domestic boilers, 'Caposil' insulating blocks, string seals on radiators) and Other (37 Fire blanket; 38 Water tank; 39 Brake/clutch lining). A red note states the diagram does not show all possible uses and locations of asbestos-containing materials and that a detailed survey will be required to identify all asbestos-containing materials present in a building.
fixes.reason: Page is printed sideways; key, numbered markers and red note read from the rotated image.
fixes.evidence: Numbered circles 1-39 on building drawing, key headings 'Roof an dexterior walls', 'Boiler, vessels and pipe work', 'Ceilings', 'Interior walls/panels', 'Flooring materials', 'Air handling systems', 'Domestic appliances', 'Other', red note box.

columns: Notes
rows: 1 Although an excavation must be inspected at the start of every shift, only one report is needed in any seven-day period. However, if something happens to affect its strength or stability, and/or an additional inspection is carried out, a report must then be completed. A record of this inspection must be made and retained for three months.

2 ‘Installation’ means putting into position and ‘assembly’ means putting together. You are not required to inspect and provide a report every time a ladder, tower scaffold or mobile elevated work platform (MEWP) is moved on site or a personal fall protection system is clipped to a new location.

3 An inspection and a report is required for a tower scaffold or MEWP (used for construction work and from which a person could fall 2 metres) after installation or assembly and every seven days thereafter, providing the equipment is being used on the same site. A record of this inspection must be made and retained for three months. If a tower scaffold is reassembled rather than simply moved, then an additional, pre-use inspection and report is required. It is acceptable for this inspection to be carried out by the person responsible for erecting the tower scaffold, providing they are trained and competent. A visible tag system, which supplements inspection records as it is updated following each pre-use inspection, is a way of recording and keeping the results until the next inspection.
4 All work equipment subject to LOLER regulation 9, thorough examination and inspection requirements, will continue to be subject to LOLER regulation 9 requirements.
